chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Jaroud, who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever intends for something of the goodness, let him hasten it, for in everything there is a delay, for the Satan therein has a glance (opportunity).'

key_terms.نَظْرَةً: a glance / a look / an opportunity

ai.seo_question: Why should one hasten in doing good deeds according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this hadith from Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) to emphasize the spiritual vulnerability that arises during the interval between intention and action. The Imam warns that Satan exploits this delay with a 'glance' (nazrah), symbolizing the subtle distraction or doubt that can extinguish the initial spark of good will. This teaching underscores the Shia emphasis on immediacy in worship to secure the deed against spiritual interference.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Abu Al Jaroud who said,

‘I heard Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The one who intends for formatting from the goodness, so let him hasten it, for in everything where is a delay, so for the Satans<sup>la</sup> therein is a respite’.
en.sarwar: 9. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sinan from abu al-Jarud who has said the following: “
I heard abu Ja’far (a.s.) say, ‘Whoever intends to perform a good deed he should do it without delay; Satan keeps an eye on anything that is delayed.’”
